# Main message

Join the free-thread union today!

CPython 3.13 free-threaded is available already for experimenting Development wheels from main Scientific Python packages are available (numpy, scipy, pandas, scikit-learn, scikit-image, ...).
# Outline ::: incremental - why should you care? - status of the Scientific Python ecosystem - road ahead? - a bit of history in scikit-learn testing ::: # Why should you care? [PEP 703](https://peps.python.org/pep-0703/) - GIL (Global Interpreter Lock) limits multithreading - multiple historical attemps to remove the GIL - this is the first one that has a chance ## multiprocessing limitations ```{.python} from joblib import Parallel, delayed results = Parallel(n_jobs=2)(delayed(worker_func)(arg) for arg in arg_list) ``` + multi-processing overhead: pickling the function, arguments and result + memory usage if you do it naively -> memmap thing in joblib + starting a process is slow -> loky keeps processes around for some time and reuses them + OpenMP not fork-safe and fork is the default start method. loky does this by doing fork+exec + alleviating overhead for small tasks: auto-grouping in joblib + pickling requirements thing don't work for interactive function i.e. defined in main or inside notebook. loky again with cloudpickle (likely). + startup of multiprocessing can be expensive 64 processes hitting the filesystem for imports on a HPC cluster ~1 minute # Status today doc: repo: ## Install Python 3.13 free-threaded today ```bash conda create -n nogil -c defaults -c ad-testing/label/py313_nogil python=3.13 ``` no conda packages for now package manager on Linux, python.org download, ... ## Install the main scientific Python packages ```{.bash} pip install \ -i https://pypi.anaconda.org/scientific-python-nightly-wheels/simple numpy ``` numpy, scipy, pandas, scikit-learn, scikit-image ... ## User report in scikit-learn - show user plots from scikit-learn user https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/issues/29587 # Road ahead?
free-threading the needle
## Notice about PEP 703 acceptance October 2023 [Notice](https://discuss.python.org/t/a-steering-council-notice-about-pep-703-making-the-global-interpreter-lock-optional-in-cpython/30474) . . . > Long-term (probably 5+ years), the no-GIL build should be the only build . . . > Before we commit to switching entirely to the no-GIL build, we need to see community support for it. . . . > We want to be very careful with backward compatibility. We do not want another Python 3 situation . . . > We want to be able to change our mind if it turns out, any time before we make no-GIL the default, that it’s just going to be too disruptive for too little gain ## Better test strategies # History of nogil/free-threaded testing in scikit-learn ## Early days 2022 - October 2021: Sam Gross announced Python 3.9 nogil fork on [python-dev](https://mail.python.org/archives/list/python-dev@python.org/thread/ABR2L6BENNA6UPSPKV474HCS4LWT26GY/) with pip-installable numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, etc ... - mid-April 2022: Olivier Grisel reports a few teething issues (segmentation faults in numpy, scipy, cython) quickly fixed by Sam Gross - single issue in scikit-learn: we used the GIL as a lock in KMeans inside OpenMP computation => replaced by an OpenMP lock - May 2022: nogil CI build with all scikit-learn test passing ## nogil 3.9 fork days 2022-July 2024 ran a few other projects tests: joblib, distributed, and reported issues scikit-learn CI: a few issues from time to time but nothing too bad very helpful answers/fixes from Sam Gross July 2023: PEP 703 [accepted](https://discuss.python.org/t/pep-703-making-the-global-interpreter-lock-optional-in-cpython-acceptance/37075/38) by the PSF Steering Committee October 2023: more [details](https://discuss.python.org/t/a-steering-council-notice-about-pep-703-making-the-global-interpreter-lock-optional-in-cpython/30474) PEP 703 acceptance by the SC ## Python 3.13 days May 2024-now - May 2024: CPython 3.13.0 beta 1 released - numpy and scipy uploaded nightly Python 3.13 free-threaded wheels to [scientific-python-nightly-wheels](https://anaconda.org/scientific-python-nightly-wheels/repo) - June 2024: scikit-learn free-threaded CI added - June 2024: free-threaded development wheel uploaded to scientific-python-nightly-wheel - most fixes in Sam Gross projects forks had been upstreamed, but a lingering one in Numpy: `RuntimeError: Identity cache already includes the item`. ## A bit more stress-testing ```{.python} import joblib # not necessarily recommended but convenient for easy testing joblib.parallel.DEFAULT_BACKEND = "threading" ``` ## Last issue found still being debugged ```{.python} # Some numbers work better than other to trigger the segmentation fault from threadpoolctl import threadpool_limits threadpool_limits(10, user_api="blas") rng = np.random.default_rng(0) L = rng.normal(size=(50, 50)) W_sr = rng.normal(size=50) def func(i): cho_solve((L, True), np.diag(W_sr)) def create_multiprocessing_pool(): # only triggers segmentation fault with multiprocessing 'fork' start_method Pool(2) if __name__ == '__main__': create_multiprocessing_pool() tpe = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) tpe.map(func, range(10)) ``` # Conclusion

Join the free-thread union today!

. . . CPython 3.13 free-threaded is available already for experimenting Development wheels from main Scientific Python packages are available (numpy, scipy, pandas, scikit-learn, scikit-image, ...). . . . How to help: setup CI for your package, test it on your use case and give feed-back . . . #
